statute_title: Driving or Operating Under the Influence of Drugs or Liquor
offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (first); Class A Misdemeanor (second); Class B Felony (third, aggravated second); Class A Felony (fourth+)
penalty_max: None beyond fine (first); 1 year (second); 3.5–7 years (third); 7.5–15 years (fourth+)
elements: Defendant drove or attempted to operate a vehicle
Upon any way or in a place to which the public has access
While under the influence of intoxicating liquor or any controlled drug
Or had a BAC of 0.08 or higher
notes: New Hampshire uses a 10-year lookback period. Implied consent under § 265-A:4. Administrative License Suspension (ALS) is separate from criminal penalties. Third DWI is a felony. Aggravated DWI (BAC ≥.16, speed ≥30 over, causing injury, child in vehicle) enhances by one class.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor
penalty_max: No jail (fine only for Class B Misdemeanor)
elements: Defendant drove or attempted to operate a vehicle
While under the influence of intoxicating liquor or drugs
BAC 0.08 or higher, or impaired driving ability
No prior DWI convictions within 10 years
mandatory_minimum: License revocation 9 months to 2 years; completion of impaired driver intervention program (IDIP)
enhancements: BAC 0.16 or higher (aggravated — Class A Misdemeanor)
notes: First offense non-aggravated is a Class B Misdemeanor — fine only, no jail. License revocation 9 months minimum. Must complete IDIP. Aggravating factors elevate to Class A Misdemeanor.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (second); Class B Felony (third); Class A Felony (fourth+)
elements: Defendant drove or attempted to operate a vehicle
While under the influence of intoxicating liquor or drugs
BAC 0.08 or higher, or impaired driving ability
One or more prior DWI convictions within 10 years
mandatory_minimum: 17 consecutive days (second, cannot be suspended); 180 days (third); 2.5 years (fourth+)
notes: Second offense: 3-year license revocation. Third offense: indefinite revocation (minimum 5 years). Fourth+: indefinite revocation (minimum 7 years). Ignition interlock required for relicensing.

offense_class: Same as alcohol DWI by offense count
penalty_max: Same as alcohol DWI by offense count
fine_max: Same as alcohol DWI by offense count
elements: Defendant drove or attempted to operate a vehicle
While under the influence of a controlled drug, prescription drug, or over-the-counter drug
Or under the combined influence of alcohol and any drug
To a degree that impaired driving ability
mandatory_minimum: Same as alcohol DWI by offense count
enhancements: Combined influence of alcohol and drugs
notes: No per se drug limits. Prosecution must show actual impairment. Drug Recognition Expert (DRE) testimony commonly used. Includes prescription medications that impair driving ability.

offense_class: Violation (first); Misdemeanor (subsequent)
elements: Defendant drove a vehicle on a way
Recklessly or in a manner that endangered or was likely to endanger any person or property
enhancements: Second or subsequent conviction within 12 months
notes: Common plea-down from DWI. First offense is a violation (fine only). Second within 12 months becomes a misdemeanor. License may be revoked for 60 days.

statute_title: Duty to Report — Accident Involving Injury or Death
offense_class: Class B Felony (injury/death); Class A Misdemeanor (property damage under § 264:25-a)
elements: Defendant was the driver of a vehicle involved in an accident
Accident resulted in injury, death, or property damage
Defendant failed to stop at the scene and provide information
Defendant failed to render reasonable assistance
notes: Leaving the scene involving injury or death is a Class B Felony. Property damage only accidents are a Class A Misdemeanor. Must remain at scene and provide name, address, and registration.

offense_class: Class A Felony (if DWI involved); Class B Felony (negligent operation)
elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
By driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs
Or by negligent operation of a motor vehicle
enhancements: DUI involved (elevated to Class A Felony under § 630:3, II)
notes: Negligent homicide while DUI is a Class A Felony. Non-DUI negligent vehicular homicide is a Class B Felony. License revocation for 7 years minimum.

offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
By negligent operation of a motor vehicle
Negligence was a gross deviation from the standard of care
notes: New Hampshire does not have a separate vehicular manslaughter statute. Vehicular deaths are charged as negligent homicide. Non-DUI related vehicular homicide is a Class B Felony.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (first); Class A Misdemeanor (second+)
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle on a public way
While defendant's license or driving privilege was suspended or revoked
Defendant had knowledge of the suspension or revocation
enhancements: Second or subsequent offense (Class A Misdemeanor)
notes: Additional 1-year extension added to suspension period. Operating after DWI-related suspension may result in additional charges and mandatory jail time.

statute_title: Disobeying an Officer — Failure to Stop
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (basic); Class B Felony (if creates serious risk)
elements: A law enforcement officer signaled the defendant to stop
Signal given by blue lights, siren, or other authorized means
Defendant willfully failed to stop or attempted to flee
Defendant knew or should have known the person was a law enforcement officer
enhancements: Creating serious risk of death or serious bodily injury (Class B Felony)
notes: Basic failure to stop is a Class A Misdemeanor. Becomes a Class B Felony if flight creates a serious risk of death or serious bodily injury to any person.

offense_class: Class B Felony (Schedule I-IV); Class A Misdemeanor (small amounts of certain drugs)
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed a controlled drug
Drug is listed on New Hampshire controlled drug schedules
Possession was without a valid prescription or lawful authority
notes: New Hampshire classifies most controlled drug possession as a Class B Felony. Drug court and diversion programs available. Marijuana possession has been partially decriminalized.

offense_class: Violation (≤3/4 oz, first/second); Class B Misdemeanor (≤3/4 oz, third+); Misdemeanor (>3/4 oz)
penalty_max: Fine only (≤3/4 oz first/second); Fine (third+); 1 year (>3/4 oz)
elements: Defendant possessed marijuana
Without lawful authority
enhancements: Third or subsequent offense (Class B Misdemeanor)
Possession of more than 3/4 ounce (misdemeanor or felony depending on amount)
notes: New Hampshire decriminalized possession of 3/4 ounce or less in 2017. First and second offenses are violations with $100 fine. Third+ becomes a Class B Misdemeanor. Larger amounts remain criminal.

offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed cocaine
Cocaine is a Schedule II controlled drug in New Hampshire
Possession was without lawful authority
notes: No minimum quantity for possession charge. Larger quantities may support sale/distribution charges.

offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed methamphetamine
Methamphetamine is a Schedule II controlled drug
Possession was without lawful authority
notes: Methamphetamine possession is prosecuted as a Class B Felony. Drug court diversion may be available for first-time offenders.

statute_title: Manufacture, Sale, or Possession with Intent — Controlled Drug
offense_class: Class A Felony (Schedule I-II, large quantities); Class B Felony (Schedule III-IV or smaller amounts)
elements: Defendant manufactured, sold, prescribed, administered, or transported a controlled drug
Or possessed with intent to sell
The substance was a controlled drug under New Hampshire law
enhancements: Sale near a school, park, or playground (§ 318-B:2-b)
Death resulting from distribution (§ 318-B:26 — up to 20 years)
notes: New Hampshire has some of the highest fines for drug trafficking in the country. Death resulting from drug distribution can add up to 20 years. Fines up to $500,000 for Class A drug felonies.

statute_title: Sale or Distribution of Controlled Drug
offense_class: Class B Felony (most); Class A Felony (large quantity Schedule I/II)
elements: Defendant sold, distributed, or dispensed a controlled drug
To another person
Knowingly or intentionally
enhancements: Death resulting from the drug sold
notes: Distribution includes any transfer of controlled drugs. Sale to minors and near schools carry enhanced penalties.

offense_class: Class A Felony (Schedule I/II); Class B Felony (Schedule III-V)
elements: Defendant manufactured, produced, or cultivated a controlled drug
Without lawful authority
Knowingly or intentionally
notes: Manufacturing methamphetamine carries additional penalties and mandatory environmental cleanup obligations.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant possessed drug paraphernalia
With knowledge of its nature and with intent to use
To introduce a controlled drug into the body
enhancements: Sale of paraphernalia to a minor (enhanced penalty)
notes: Possession of hypodermic syringes was decriminalized by New Hampshire's syringe services program. Paraphernalia for injection may not be prosecuted under harm reduction policies.

offense_class: Class B Felony (most); Class A Felony (large quantity Schedule I/II)
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed a controlled drug
With intent to sell, distribute, or dispense
Intent inferred from quantity, packaging, scales, cash, or other evidence
notes: Intent to sell is inferred from circumstances. Penalties are the same as for actual distribution.

offense_class: Capital/Unclassified Felony
elements: Defendant purposely caused the death of another
After deliberation and premeditation
Or killed during the commission of certain felonies (felony murder)
enhancements: Victim was a law enforcement officer or judicial officer
Felony murder (during kidnapping, rape, robbery, arson, burglary)
notes: New Hampshire repealed the death penalty in 2019 (override of governor's veto). Mandatory sentence is life without parole. Felony murder applies to killings during specified dangerous felonies.

offense_class: Class A Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly caused the death of another person
Without deliberation and premeditation
Or recklessly caused the death under circumstances manifesting extreme indifference to human life
mandatory_minimum: 18 years minimum before parole eligibility (if firearm used)
enhancements: Use of a firearm (mandatory minimum 18 years before parole)
notes: Second-degree murder is a Class A Felony with potential life sentence. Parole eligibility exists unlike first-degree murder. Minimum parole eligibility is typically 18 years.

offense_class: Class A Felony
elements: Defendant recklessly caused the death of another person
Or caused the death while under the influence of extreme mental or emotional disturbance
For which there was a reasonable explanation
notes: Manslaughter covers both reckless killing and heat-of-passion killing. The reasonableness of the emotional disturbance is determined from the viewpoint of a reasonable person in the defendant's situation.

offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
Through criminal negligence
A gross deviation from the standard of care a reasonable person would exercise
notes: Involuntary manslaughter in New Hampshire is a Class B Felony. Requires more than ordinary negligence — must be a gross deviation from the standard of care.

offense_class: Class A Felony (serious bodily injury); Class B Felony (with deadly weapon)
elements: Defendant purposely caused serious bodily injury to another
Or purposely or knowingly caused bodily injury to another by means of a deadly weapon
Or knowingly caused injury while committing or attempting certain felonies
enhancements: Use of a deadly weapon (minimum Class B Felony)
Against a law enforcement officer or emergency personnel
Victim suffered permanent disfigurement or disability
notes: First-degree assault is New Hampshire's most serious assault charge below homicide. Strangulation causing loss of consciousness is specifically included as a Class A Felony.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (bodily contact/injury); Class B Misdemeanor (unprivileged physical contact only)
elements: Defendant purposely or knowingly caused bodily injury or unprivileged physical contact to another
Or recklessly caused bodily injury to another
Or negligently caused bodily injury to another by means of a deadly weapon
enhancements: Against a person under 13 years old (enhanced under § 631:2-a, II(a))
notes: Simple assault causing bodily injury is a Class A Misdemeanor. Mere unprivileged physical contact without injury is a Class B Misdemeanor.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant purposely or knowingly caused bodily injury to another
Through physical contact
notes: New Hampshire does not have a separate battery statute. Harmful physical contact is prosecuted as simple assault.

offense_class: Class B Felony (basic); Class A Felony (armed or injury)
elements: Defendant committed theft
In the course of committing the theft, defendant used physical force or threatened imminent use of force
Against the person of the owner or anyone present
With the purpose of preventing resistance or compelling delivery
enhancements: Armed with a deadly weapon (Class A Felony under § 636:1, III(a))
Inflicting or attempting to inflict death or serious bodily injury (Class A Felony)
notes: Basic robbery is a Class B Felony. Armed robbery or robbery causing serious injury is a Class A Felony.

offense_class: Class A Felony
elements: Defendant committed robbery
While armed with a deadly weapon
Or inflicted or attempted to inflict death or serious bodily injury
notes: Armed robbery is a Class A Felony. The deadly weapon need not be used — merely being armed during the robbery is sufficient.

offense_class: Class A Felony (general); Class B Felony (if victim released unharmed in safe place)
elements: Defendant knowingly confined another person
With purpose to hold for ransom or as a shield or hostage
Or to facilitate commission of a felony
Or to inflict bodily injury, terrorize, or interfere with governmental function
notes: Reduced to Class B Felony if defendant voluntarily releases victim alive and unharmed in a safe place before trial.

offense_class: Class A Felony (occupied structure/danger to life); Class B Felony (unoccupied structure)
elements: Defendant knowingly started a fire or caused an explosion
Which unlawfully damaged or destroyed the property of another
Or the defendant's own property under circumstances endangering others
enhancements: Occupied structure at time of fire (Class A Felony)
Person endangered or injured (Class A Felony)
notes: Class A Felony when anyone is in danger. Class B Felony for property damage without danger to life. Separate offense for failure to control or report a fire under § 634:2.

offense_class: Class A Felony
penalty_max: 7.5–15 years (or up to life if court finds exceptional circumstances)
elements: Defendant purposely engaged in conduct constituting a substantial step
Toward the commission of first-degree murder
With the intent to kill another person
notes: Attempted murder carries the same felony class as the completed offense minus one degree, but attempted first-degree murder remains a Class A Felony.

offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant purposely or knowingly caused bodily injury to another
By means of a deadly weapon
enhancements: Serious bodily injury (elevated to Class A Felony)
notes: Assault with a deadly weapon causing bodily injury is a Class B Felony. If serious bodily injury results, it becomes a Class A Felony.

statute_title: Theft by Unauthorized Taking or Transfer
offense_class: Class A Felony (>$1,500); Class B Felony ($1,001–$1,500); Class A Misdemeanor (≤$1,000)
penalty_max: 7.5–15 years (Class A); 3.5–7 years (Class B); 1 year (Class A Misdemeanor)
elements: Defendant obtained or exercised unauthorized control over the property of another
With purpose to deprive the owner of the property
enhancements: Theft of a firearm (felony regardless of value)
notes: New Hampshire grades theft primarily by value. Theft of a firearm is always a Class B Felony regardless of value. Multiple thefts may be aggregated.

offense_class: Class A Felony (>$1,500); Class B Felony ($1,001–$1,500)
elements: Defendant committed theft as defined in RSA 637
Value of property exceeded $1,000
notes: New Hampshire does not use the term 'grand theft.' Felony theft begins at $1,001.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant committed theft as defined in RSA 637
Value of property was $1,000 or less
notes: Misdemeanor theft applies for property valued at $1,000 or less. Prior theft convictions may be considered at sentencing.

offense_class: Same grading as general theft by value
penalty_max: Same as general theft by value
fine_max: Same as general theft by value
elements: Defendant willfully concealed merchandise of a store
While on or off the premises
With intent to steal without paying the purchase price
enhancements: Use of anti-shoplifting device removal tools
notes: New Hampshire has a specific willful concealment statute for shoplifting. Civil recovery by merchants also available. Penalty grading follows general theft thresholds.

offense_class: Class B Felony (general); Class A Felony (armed or nighttime dwelling)
elements: Defendant entered a building or occupied structure
Or separately secured or occupied section thereof
With purpose to commit a crime therein
enhancements: Armed with a deadly weapon (Class A Felony)
Nighttime entry of a dwelling (Class A Felony)
Inflicts or attempts to inflict bodily injury (Class A Felony)
notes: Basic burglary is a Class B Felony. Elevated to Class A Felony if defendant is armed, enters a dwelling at night, or causes injury.

statute_title: Burglary — Dwelling at Night (Class A Felony)
offense_class: Class A Felony
elements: Defendant entered a dwelling
During nighttime hours
With purpose to commit a crime therein
notes: Nighttime entry of a dwelling is always a Class A Felony regardless of whether anyone was present.

offense_class: Class A Felony (most vehicles exceed $1,500)
elements: Defendant obtained or exercised unauthorized control over a motor vehicle of another
With purpose to deprive the owner of the vehicle
enhancements: Vehicle used in commission of another felony
notes: Motor vehicle theft is graded by value under general theft statutes. Most vehicles exceed the $1,500 Class A Felony threshold.

offense_class: Same grading as general theft by value
penalty_max: Same as general theft by value
fine_max: Same as general theft by value
elements: Defendant received, retained, or disposed of property of another
Knowing it was stolen or believing it was probably stolen
With the purpose to deprive the owner
notes: Graded by value of stolen property. Belief that property is probably stolen is sufficient — absolute knowledge not required.

offense_class: Class B Felony (>$1,500); Class A Misdemeanor ($100–$1,500); Class B Misdemeanor (<$100)
penalty_max: 3.5–7 years (Class B Felony); 1 year (Class A Misdemeanor); fine only (Class B Misdemeanor)
elements: Defendant purposely or recklessly damaged property of another
Or purposely or recklessly tampered with property so as to endanger persons or property
enhancements: Damage to utilities or public infrastructure
notes: New Hampshire uses 'criminal mischief' for vandalism. Graded by the amount of damage. Restitution commonly ordered.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (occupied structure); Class B Misdemeanor (other premises)
elements: Defendant knowingly entered or remained in a place
Without license or privilege to do so
After being notified not to enter or to leave
enhancements: Trespass in an occupied structure (Class A Misdemeanor)
notes: Trespass in an occupied structure is a Class A Misdemeanor. Trespass on other premises (land) is a Class B Misdemeanor.

offense_class: Class B Felony to Class B Misdemeanor (graded by damage amount)
penalty_max: 3.5–7 years (Class B Felony); 1 year (Class A Misdemeanor); fine only (Class B Misdemeanor)
elements: Defendant purposely or recklessly damaged property of another
Or purposely or recklessly tampered with property of another
So as to endanger persons or property
notes: Same statute as vandalism. Criminal mischief includes tampering with utilities, transportation, and communication systems.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (simple); Class B Felony (second+ or with deadly weapon); Class A Felony (serious bodily injury)
penalty_max: 1 year (misdemeanor); 3.5–7 years (Class B Felony); 7.5–15 years (Class A Felony)
elements: Defendant committed an assault against a family or household member
Or intimate partner
Family or household member includes spouse, former spouse, cohabitant, parent of shared child
enhancements: Second or subsequent offense (Class B Felony under § 631:2-b, III)
Use of a deadly weapon (first-degree assault applies)
notes: New Hampshire enacted domestic violence-specific assault statute. Second or subsequent domestic violence assault is a Class B Felony. Strangulation is specifically addressed.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant purposely or knowingly caused bodily injury to a family or household member
Or recklessly caused bodily injury to a family or household member
First offense
enhancements: Second or subsequent offense (Class B Felony)
notes: Court may order batterer intervention program. Victim eligible for protective order under RSA 173-B.

statute_title: Endangering Welfare of a Child or Incompetent
offense_class: Class B Felony (child under 18); Misdemeanor (less serious circumstances)
elements: Defendant knowingly endangered the welfare of a child under 18
By violating a duty of care, protection, or support
Or by inducing, aiding, or encouraging the child to engage in delinquent conduct
notes: Includes DWI with child in vehicle, exposure to drugs or violence, and failure to provide necessities.

statute_title: Assault on a Child / Child Abuse
offense_class: Class A Felony (serious bodily injury); Class B Felony (bodily injury with deadly weapon); Class A Misdemeanor (simple assault)
penalty_max: 7.5–15 years (Class A); 3.5–7 years (Class B); 1 year (Class A Misdemeanor)
elements: Defendant caused bodily injury to a child
Purposely, knowingly, or recklessly
Injury was not the result of reasonable parental discipline
notes: Child abuse is prosecuted under general assault statutes with age as an aggravating factor, or under the endangering welfare statute. DCYF involvement accompanies criminal prosecution.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (first); Class B Felony (subsequent or with assault)
elements: A valid protective order was in effect under RSA 173-B
Defendant had knowledge of the order
Defendant knowingly violated a provision of the order
notes: Law enforcement must arrest upon probable cause of violation. Subsequent violation or violation involving physical contact is a Class B Felony.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (first); Class B Felony (second+ or with credible threat)
elements: Defendant purposely, on more than one occasion, followed, contacted, or placed under surveillance another person
Without legitimate purpose
Causing the person to fear for their safety
enhancements: Second or subsequent offense (Class B Felony)
Threat of death or serious bodily injury
Violation of a protective order while stalking
notes: Includes electronic surveillance and cyberstalking. Second offense or stalking with credible threat is a Class B Felony.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (most); Violation (single incident telephone harassment)
elements: Defendant, with purpose to annoy or alarm another
Communicated threats, insults, or taunts
Or made repeated communications at extremely inconvenient hours or in offensive language
notes: Includes telephone harassment and electronic harassment. Repeated conduct may support stalking charges.

statute_title: Criminal Neglect of Elderly, Disabled, or Impaired Adults
offense_class: Class A Felony (serious bodily injury/death); Class B Felony (bodily injury); Class A Misdemeanor (general neglect)
penalty_max: 7.5–15 years (Class A); 3.5–7 years (Class B); 1 year (Class A Misdemeanor)
elements: Defendant knowingly or recklessly caused serious bodily injury or neglect to an elderly or disabled adult
Elderly is 60 years of age or older
Defendant had a duty of care for the adult
notes: New Hampshire has specific criminal neglect provisions for elderly and disabled adults. Bureau of Elderly and Adult Services investigates.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (general); Class B Felony (certain prohibited circumstances)
elements: Defendant carried or possessed a firearm
Under circumstances prohibited by law
Such as while intoxicated, in a courthouse, or as a prohibited person
enhancements: Possession in a prohibited location (courthouse, school)
notes: New Hampshire does not require a permit for concealed carry (constitutional carry since 2017). Restrictions remain for prohibited persons and certain locations.

statute_title: Possession of Firearm by Convicted Felon
offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant possessed a firearm
Defendant had been convicted of a felony against the person or property of another
Or defendant had been convicted of a felony drug offense
enhancements: Use of firearm in commission of another offense
notes: New Hampshire restricts felon possession more narrowly than federal law — applies primarily to violent felons and drug felons. Some felons may petition for restoration of rights.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (general); Class B Felony (courtroom)
elements: Defendant carried a firearm
In a location where firearms are prohibited
Such as a courtroom (§ 159:19) or while intoxicated
notes: Constitutional carry state — few location restrictions. Courtroom carry is a felony. Federal property, schools (federal law), and private property restrictions apply.

statute_title: Firing Guns Near Buildings, Highways, or in Compact Areas
offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (general); Class A Misdemeanor (if endangering persons)
elements: Defendant discharged a firearm
Within 300 feet of a permanently occupied dwelling, public building, or highway
Without the property owner's permission
notes: New Hampshire has specific distance requirements for firearm discharge near buildings and highways. Discharge in compact areas is separately regulated by municipalities.

offense_class: Class A Felony (posing as another to evade detection or liability); Class B Felony (general identity fraud)
elements: Defendant knowingly posed as another person
Or used the personal identifying information of another without authorization
To obtain credit, goods, services, or anything of value, or to avoid detection
notes: New Hampshire's identity fraud statute covers a broad range of identity theft conduct. Restitution commonly ordered.

offense_class: Same grading as general theft by value
penalty_max: Same as general theft by value
fine_max: Same as general theft by value
elements: Defendant was entrusted with property of another
Defendant obtained or exercised unauthorized control over the property
With purpose to deprive the owner
notes: New Hampshire prosecutes embezzlement under the general theft statute. The fiduciary or employment relationship is the distinguishing element.

offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant falsely made, completed, or altered a writing
With purpose to defraud or deceive
So that it purported to be the act of another or to have been executed at a different time or place
notes: Forgery is always a Class B Felony in New Hampshire. Includes checks, deeds, contracts, and identification documents.

statute_title: Fraudulent Handling of Recordable Writings / Counterfeiting
offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant falsely made, manufactured, or possessed counterfeit instruments
Including currency, securities, or identification documents
With intent to deceive or defraud
notes: Counterfeiting of federal currency is typically prosecuted federally. New Hampshire's forgery statutes cover state-level counterfeiting.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (general); Class B Felony (>$1,500)
elements: Defendant issued or passed a check or other negotiable instrument
Knowing it would not be honored by the drawee
Or having insufficient funds and failing to make good within 14 days of notice
notes: Failure to make good within 14 days of dishonor notice creates a presumption of knowledge. Graded by the amount of the check.

offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly presented or caused to be presented a false or fraudulent claim
For payment under an insurance policy
With intent to defraud
notes: New Hampshire Insurance Fraud Investigation Unit investigates. Restitution and civil penalties may apply in addition to criminal penalties.

statute_title: Fraudulent Use of a Credit Card
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (≤$1,000); Class B Felony (>$1,000)
elements: Defendant used a credit card, debit card, or account number of another
Without authorization
To obtain goods, services, or anything of value
With intent to defraud
notes: New Hampshire has a specific credit card fraud statute. Graded by value obtained.

offense_class: Class A Felony
elements: Defendant conducted or attempted to conduct a financial transaction
Knowing the property involved represented proceeds of drug trafficking
With intent to promote criminal activity or conceal the source of funds
notes: New Hampshire's money laundering provisions are primarily connected to drug trafficking proceeds. Federal money laundering charges may also apply.

offense_class: Same grading as general theft by value
penalty_max: Same as general theft by value
fine_max: Same as general theft by value
elements: Defendant obtained property of another by deception
By creating or reinforcing a false impression
Including false impressions of law, value, intention, or other state of mind
notes: New Hampshire's general fraud offense is theft by deception. Graded by value of property obtained.

offense_class: Class A Felony
penalty_max: 10–20 years minimum to life (victim under 13); 7.5–15 years (other)
elements: Defendant engaged in sexual penetration with another person
By force, threat of force, or coercion
Or when the victim was unable to consent due to age, disability, or incapacity
enhancements: Victim under 13 (mandatory 10–20 years minimum, 25 years to life)
notes: Aggravated felonious sexual assault is New Hampshire's most serious sexual offense. Victim under 13 triggers mandatory minimum of 10–20 years with maximum of 25 years to life.

offense_class: Class A Felony
elements: Defendant engaged in sexual penetration with another person
Without the victim's consent
Through force, threat of force, or other coercive circumstance
notes: New Hampshire does not use the term 'rape' in its statutes. What other states call rape is prosecuted as aggravated felonious sexual assault.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (first); Class B Felony (second+)
elements: Defendant fornicates, exposes genitals, or performs any other act of gross lewdness
Under circumstances which the defendant should know will likely cause affront or alarm
enhancements: Second or subsequent offense (Class B Felony)
Exposure to a person under 16 (Class B Felony)
notes: First offense is a Class A Misdemeanor. Second or subsequent offense is a Class B Felony. Exposure to a child under 16 is always a Class B Felony.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (first); Class A Misdemeanor (second+)
elements: Defendant engaged in or agreed to engage in sexual contact in return for consideration
Or defendant solicited another to engage in sexual contact for consideration
enhancements: Second or subsequent offense (Class A Misdemeanor)
notes: Both the person soliciting and the person offering are subject to prosecution. Promoting prostitution is a separate, more serious offense under § 645:2, II.

statute_title: Manufacture, Distribution, or Possession of Child Sexual Abuse Images
offense_class: Class A Felony (manufacture/distribution); Class B Felony (possession of 3+ images); Class A Misdemeanor (1–2 images)
penalty_max: 7.5–15 years (Class A); 3.5–7 years (Class B); 1 year (Class A Misdemeanor)
elements: Defendant knowingly manufactured, distributed, or possessed visual representations of child sexual abuse
Involving a child under 18
Defendant knew or should have known the subject was a child
enhancements: 3 or more images (Class B Felony minimum)
notes: New Hampshire uses the term 'child sexual abuse images' rather than 'child pornography.' Each image may constitute a separate count.

statute_title: Failure to Register as Sex Offender
offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant was required to register under the Sex Offender Registration Act
Defendant knowingly failed to register, verify, or update registration
Or provided false registration information
enhancements: Second or subsequent failure to register
notes: New Hampshire requires sex offender registration for 10 years, 20 years, or lifetime depending on the offense tier. Verification required every 90 days to annually.

offense_class: Class B Felony (13–15 and defendant 4+ years older); Class A Felony (under 13)
penalty_max: 3.5–7 years (Class B); 25 years to life (under 13 with penetration)
elements: Defendant engaged in sexual contact or penetration with a person under 16
Defendant was 4 or more years older than the victim
Consent is not a defense due to victim's age
enhancements: Victim under 13 (Class A Felony with mandatory minimum)
notes: New Hampshire age of consent is 16. The 4-year age difference threshold applies. Victims under 13 face the most severe penalties under § 632-A:2.

offense_class: Violation (general); Class B Misdemeanor (certain circumstances)
penalty_max: Fine only (violation); Fine only (Class B Misdemeanor)
elements: Defendant purposely caused a breach of the peace
By violent, tumultuous, or threatening behavior
Or by creating a hazardous condition by an act not serving a legitimate purpose
notes: New Hampshire disorderly conduct is a minor offense — typically a violation (fine only). Often used as a plea-down.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant knowingly or purposely physically interfered with a person
Recognized as a law enforcement official
Seeking to effect an arrest or detention
Regardless of whether the arrest or detention was legal
notes: Physical interference required — verbal refusal alone is not sufficient. Applies regardless of whether the underlying arrest was lawful.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant used force, violence, intimidation, or physical interference
Or committed any independently unlawful act
With purpose to interfere with a public servant performing an official function
notes: Broader than resisting arrest. Covers interference with any government function. Includes providing false information to officials.

offense_class: Varies (civil vs. criminal)
penalty_max: Varies (up to jail until compliance for civil; defined sentence for criminal)
elements: Defendant engaged in disorderly conduct in the presence of the court
Or disobeyed a lawful order of the court
Or willfully violated a court directive
notes: Direct contempt may be punished summarily. Indirect contempt requires notice and hearing. Criminal contempt is punitive; civil contempt is coercive.

offense_class: Violation
elements: Defendant was found intoxicated on a street, highway, or public place
Or on licensed premises where alcoholic beverages are sold
notes: Minor offense — violation level with fine only. Many jurisdictions use protective custody rather than prosecution.

statute_title: Default or Breach of Bail Conditions — Failure to Appear
offense_class: Class B Felony (if underlying charge is felony); Class A Misdemeanor (if underlying charge is misdemeanor)
elements: Defendant was released on bail or personal recognizance
Defendant was required to appear before a court
Defendant failed to appear as required
notes: Penalty based on seriousness of underlying charge. Court issues a bench warrant. Bail is forfeited.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (false crime report); Class B Misdemeanor (false alarm)
elements: Defendant knowingly gave false information to a law enforcement officer
About the commission of a crime or other incident
With purpose to induce investigation or other action
notes: Includes false reports of crimes and false emergency calls. Defendant may be liable for investigation costs.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (general); Class B Felony (deadly weapon displayed or victim believes death is imminent)
elements: Defendant threatened to commit a crime against another
By placing the person in fear that the crime would be committed
With the purpose of terrorizing the person
enhancements: Display of a deadly weapon (Class B Felony)
Threat placing victim in fear of imminent death (Class B Felony)
Threat against a school or public building
notes: Basic criminal threatening is a Class A Misdemeanor. Elevated to Class B Felony when a deadly weapon is displayed or when the threat places the victim in fear of imminent death.

offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant made a material false statement under oath or equivalent affirmation
In an official proceeding
Defendant did not believe the statement to be true
notes: Requires proof the statement was material to the proceeding. Retraction before discovery is an affirmative defense.

statute_title: Bribery in Official and Political Matters
offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant offered, conferred, or agreed to confer a benefit
Upon a public servant
As consideration for the public servant's decision, vote, or action in an official matter
notes: Both offering and accepting bribes are criminal offenses. Public servant includes all government officials and employees.

offense_class: Class B Felony (from felony custody); Class A Misdemeanor (from misdemeanor custody)
elements: Defendant was in official custody
Defendant removed themselves from custody without authorization
Or failed to return from authorized temporary absence
enhancements: Use of force or threat of force
notes: Penalty graded by seriousness of underlying offense. Sentence may be consecutive to original sentence.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (general); Class B Felony (torture, fighting, or death of animal)
elements: Defendant knowingly tortured, beat, mutilated, or cruelly treated an animal
Or caused or procured such treatment
Or knowingly failed to provide necessary food, water, shelter, or veterinary care
enhancements: Torture or causing death (Class B Felony under § 644:8, III-a)
notes: General animal cruelty is a Class A Misdemeanor. Torture, mutilation causing death, and animal fighting are Class B Felonies.

offense_class: Depends on underlying offense
penalty_max: Original suspended sentence may be imposed
elements: Defendant was placed on probation
Defendant violated a condition of probation
Violation was established at a revocation hearing
enhancements: New criminal offense while on probation
notes: Court may revoke probation and impose original sentence, continue probation, or modify conditions. Burden of proof is preponderance of the evidence.

offense_class: Depends on underlying offense
elements: Defendant was released on parole
Defendant violated a condition of parole
Violation was established at a revocation hearing
notes: Adult Parole Board makes revocation decisions. May revoke parole and return offender to prison for remaining sentence.

statute_title: Criminal Liability for Conduct of Another
offense_class: Same as principal offense
elements: Defendant, acting with the kind of culpability required for the offense
Caused another to engage in the prohibited conduct
Or aided, agreed to aid, or attempted to aid another in planning or committing the offense
notes: An accomplice is legally accountable for the conduct of the principal. New Hampshire holds accomplices to the same level of liability.

offense_class: One class below the completed offense (attempts to commit Class A Felonies remain Class A Felonies)
penalty_max: Varies by class of attempted offense
fine_max: Varies by class of attempted offense
elements: Defendant, acting with the kind of culpability otherwise required for the offense
Purposely engaged in conduct constituting a substantial step
Toward the commission of the crime
notes: Attempt to commit a Class A Felony is a Class A Felony. All other attempts are graded one class below the completed offense. Voluntary abandonment is an affirmative defense.

offense_class: One class below the target offense (conspiracy to commit Class A Felony remains Class A Felony)
penalty_max: Varies by class of target offense
fine_max: Varies by class of target offense
elements: Defendant agreed with one or more persons to commit or cause the commission of a crime
Defendant or a co-conspirator committed an overt act in furtherance of the agreement
Defendant had the purpose that the crime be committed
notes: Conspiracy to commit a Class A Felony is a Class A Felony. All other conspiracies are graded one class below the target offense. Requires at least one overt act.
